newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says EU pact will prevent new Vilvoorde.
newsitem.headline: France says EU pact will prevent new Vilvoorde.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Monday the European Union's newly signed pact on jobs would avoid the kind of outcry created by the proposed closure of a Renault car plant in Belgium.

Strauss-Kahn, speaking on French television from Amsterdam where the growth and employment pact was signed, claimed credit for efforts to prevent a repeat of the closure plan, which sparked union outrage in both France and Belgium.

"In the resolution which has now been signed, I insisted something should be introduced which prevents this type of operation -- which prevents a lack of consultation with unions or procedures that are excessively short," Strauss-Kahn said.
"This has now been accepted and does not even have to wait until the next summit," he said, referring to plans for a special Luxembourg jobs summit in the autumn.
Strauss-Kahn did not say what parts of the EU deal he was referring to. But an extract from Monday's resolution called for existing EU laws to be used while respecting national standards.

"The European Council recommends social dialogue and the full use of present Community law concerning the consultation of social partners, including, where relevant, in processes of restructuring, and taking into account national practices," a text of the resolution released in Amsterdam said.
A resolution from EU leaders has no legal force but carries a strong political signal to officials.
Renault announced in February that it planned to shut down its loss-making Vilvoorde plant, where about 2,900 people have jobs.

But the company, still 46 percent-owned by the French state after privatisation, appeared to bow pressure from the new Socialist government a week ago when it agreed to order an independent study to seek alternatives to closure.
